⏺ The review finished. Before relaying it, I checked the two blocking errors
  myself, and both hold up:
  - A-1: I had already confirmed the Transmogulate mismatch.
  - A-2 case (a): with Going Long's Armor 2, each CN-Virus deals 0 damage but
    still adds 2 copies. A library of only viruses therefore grows by 1 per draw
    and never runs out.
  - A-2 case (b): Unstable Clone Machine copies each drawn Hinder 3 times, so a
    library of only Hinders grows by 2 per draw.

  its own list of `play`-action fields (A-3), R78's `memory` reset strips Heroic
  Power's rolled power with no re-roll rule (A-4), and R79 gives no clock rule
  for a prompt owned by the non-active player (A-5).

    ## Suggested fixes (BLOCKER and MAJOR; not applied)
    - A-1: R77: replace "The ingredients cease to exist" with "The non-target
  ingredient ceases to exist with no Death trigger and without counting as
  destroyed; the target's instance survives as the fused card." Cite in #85 and
  #99.
    - A-2: Add to R61 (or R77): "Immutable permanents are never chosen as a Fuse
  target; if no legal target of that type remains, Unlicensed Experimentation
  fires and is consumed with no effect (as R17 for Sheepish), and the played
  permanent stays."
    - A-3: Either add `handPicks[]` and `direction` to the `play` action in
  §10.2/§10.9 and keep #26 and #52 in R81, or drop #26 and #52 from R81's "Cards
  affected" and state in R81 that `hand`, `discover` and `direction` choices
  always open a `PendingChoice`.
    - A-4: R43: "A Heroic Power with no `memory.power` rolls one the moment it
  enters any hand or library." Alternatively exclude `memory.power` from R78's
  reset list and cite #98 in R78's "Cards affected".
    - A-5: R79/§9.5: "The turn clock belongs to the active player and pauses
  while a prompt is open for the non-active player, which runs on its own
  `PROMPT_CLOCK`; `timeout` answers only prompts belonging to the player whose
  clock expired."

    Fixed since the third run: M5-T2 now builds `direction` into the play action
  per R81 and #26's must-pass says the hand card is "picked as part of the play
  rather than a prompt (R81)"; #98 covers a copy created mid-game, a mulliganed
  one and a bounced one (R43); #85 carries the Immutable rule, the
  no-legal-target consumption and the surviving-target semantics (R61, R77); #99
  states "no on-field target (R77)"; BUILD:119 adds the server constants
  `TURN_CLOCK_SECONDS` 75, `PROMPT_CLOCK_SECONDS` 30, `DISCONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS`
  60, `MATCH_CEILING_MINUTES` 60, `ROOM_CODE_LENGTH` 6, `ELO_K` 32, `ELO_START`
  1000; M7-T1 distinguishes a prompt held by the non-active player and pauses
  the turn clock (R79); e2e/02 exercises all ten pickers "whether it builds the
  `play` action or answers a `PendingChoice` (R81)". The event lists still match
  exactly (40 = 40, verified by script), and M4-T2's three pools match my A2.5
  recount.

    Remaining:
    1. BUILD:255 (M3-T7 `fuse.ts`) still says "the result keeps the target's
  state; **the ingredients cease to exist**", the exact pairing the third run
  flagged as SPEC A-1; R77 and BUILD:386 (#85) now say only the *other*
  ingredients do.
    2. BUILD:143 (M1-T3) accepts "An action other than `answer` while

    **The trigger-controller bug fix is real and I confirm it.**
  `triggerOrder(sink, hook, only?)` (turn.ts:21) now takes a controller filter
  and both call sites pass the active player (turn.ts:91 `startOfTurn`,
  turn.ts:121 `endOfTurn`). This was a genuine rules defect: start- and
  end-of-turn hooks previously fired for both sides every turn, which
  contradicts §6.2 ("Controller's turn start"/"Controller's turn end") and would
  have broken #13 ("not on the opponent's end"), #6, #9, #37, #40, #58, #59,
  #65, #71, #91 and #93. The regression test turn.test.ts:142 `it("fires a
  start-of-turn trigger on its controller's turn only (§6.2)")` proves both
  directions — the graveyard is untouched on p2's turn and emptied on p1's. The
  design is also right for what comes next: keeping the unfiltered `only ===
  undefined` path means the M4 end-of-turn trap window can still fire Bread and
  Butter and Intern Stimmy on **both** sides in R68 order, as R62 requires.
  (That branch consequently has no caller yet — expected, not a defect.)

    ## `queryCost` (R65, SPEC.md:789)
    Out-of-play cost: a number cost as printed (Ceaseless Void's 100 included),
  `"X"` → 0, an embiggen cost → its `base` price. Documented as the def-level
  counterpart to `mana.effectiveCost`, which is the in-play calculation from an
  instance.

    ## `CatalogQueryArgs` fields and who needs each
    From `CatalogQuery` (packages/shared/src/catalog-types.ts:110):
    - `set` — scorer.ts:73 (`{ set: "Core", excludeIndex: ZEPHYRS_INDEX }`),
  rulings-b.test.ts:686
    - `excludeIndex` — scorer.ts:73 and effects/choose.ts:186-190 (the
  self-index exclusion in `discoverFromCatalog`); accepts one index or an array
    - `tags` — callToChaos.ts:238 (`{ tags: [CHAOS_TAG] }`),
  effects-choose.test.ts (`{ tags: ["Fruit"] }`), rulings-b.test.ts:687 (`{
  tags: ["Token"] }`)
    - `type` — callToChaos.ts:129 (`{ type: "Unit", cost: 3 }`) and
  CHAOS_BACKROW_QUERY (`type: ["Field Spell","Trap","Field Trap"]`),
  rulings-b.test.ts:365/693/857
    - `cost` — callToChaos.ts:129, effects-choose.test.ts:333 (`{ cost: 99 }` →
  empty pool, fizzles)
    - `notTags`, `costRange`, `rarity` — not passed by any current caller but
  named by SPEC §5.1 (SPEC.md:215) and used by the §8 #7 row (`{cost,
  notTags:[Token], excludeIndex:7}`), so they are implemented.

    Added beyond `CatalogQuery` (no current call site passes them; they mirror
  `RecruitFilter` in effects/summon.ts:151 so a card can hand the same filter
  shape to Recruit or to a pool, and they are how a card "names its own pool"
  per §5.1):
    - `index` / `notIndex` (index-named pool; `notIndex` is the inverse of the
  §5.1-spelled `excludeIndex`, both honoured)
    - `defId` (pool built from ids a script already holds)
    - `token` (`true` asks for tokens only, `false` forbids them — the default
  already does)

    Semantics implemented exactly as specified: `tags` = has every listed tag;
  `notTags` = has none; `costRange` inclusive; `cost`/`costRange` compared
  against `queryCost(def)` (R65, so X reads 0 and an embiggen card its base
  price); `excludeIndex`/`notIndex`/`index`/`defId`/`type`/`rarity` accept a
  scalar or an array.

    Token gate (§5.1, SPEC.md:211): tokens (`def.token === true` or a `"Token"`
  tag) are dropped unless the args name that pool — `tags` includes `"Token"`,
  `rarity` includes `"Token"`, `token: true`, or `index`/`defId` names members
  outright. Only the registered catalog is searched, so fused/crafted
  `transientDefs` can never be generated by a pool.

    Deterministic order: sorted by §5 index as a strict total order — index
  parsed as a number ascending (non-numeric token indexes like `"T-rush"` last),
  then the index string, then the unique catalog id. So the result never
  depends on registry key order and a seeded `rng.pick`/`rng.shuffle` over it
  replays identically (R58, R60, §9.3).

    Behaviour spot-checked with a throwaway tsx probe in the scratchpad (all
  correct): `query({})` = index order `2,3,4,5,10` with the token dropped;
  `query({set:"Core"})` token-free; `query({tags:["Token"]})` and
  `query({token:true})` return the token; `query({cost:0})` finds the X card;
  `query({cost:2})` finds the embiggen card at its base price;
  costRange/tags/notTags/type/rarity/index/defId/notIndex/multi-excludeIndex all
  as contracted; `queryCost` = 1 / 2 / 0 / 100.

    ## Judgements made

    1. **`radiant` = `base` on all four.** Confirmed by SPEC §5.2's final
  bullet: "Cards with no listed Radiant form (Quickstriker, Zao Gao,
  Combo-Fodder, Chaos Golem, My Pawn, and the Rush, Sheep, Felinor and Bread
  Tokens) are unchanged by becoming Radiant; the flag still sets so counting
  effects behave." BUILD M4-T1's acceptance bullet names the same set by index:
  "#38, #80, #93.1, #95.1, #96 and the shared tokens" — and §8 confirms #38 =
  Quickstriker, #96 = My Pawn, so the two lists agree card-for-card. Faces are
  byte-identical, not just numerically equal, so a `toEqual` on the whole face
  passes.

    2. **Felinor Token tag order — the one place I had to choose, please
  reconcile.** I used `["Token", "Felinor"]`, following your schema comment
  (`"tags": ["Token"], // plus any tribe`) and the existing engine fixture
  helper `tokenDef(name, tags: Tag[] = ["Token"])` in `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documen
  ts/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine/test/fixtures/catalog.ts:44`, which
  puts Token first. **But §8's own "Type, tags" cells list the tribe before
  Token** — `51.1` reads "Spell, KY, Token" and `90.1` reads "Spell, CN, Token".
  If the four agents transcribing the N.1 tokens read those cells literally
  they will produce `["KY","Token"]` and `["CN","Token"]`, i.e. tribe-first,
  which is the opposite order from mine. Array order matters to a deep-equality
  fixture test, so pick one convention for the merged catalog. §7 is no help:
  its cell is "Unit, Felinor", which is type-then-tribe with no Token at all (§7
  leaves the Token tag implicit — §5's Index row and §7's Bread ruling say
  every token counts as a Token for every filter).

    3. **Bread Token stats vs text.** §7's cell: "Printed 0/0; always summoned
  as X/X through `statsOverride` (X = unspent mana, or 3X); no text". I put the
  literal printed 0/0 in `attack`/`health` and no `X` anywhere in the stat
  fields; the X/X rule lives in `text`. R37 ("Named Bread Token, cost 0, no
  text") and BUILD's row T ("Bread is X/X with no text") both back cost 0 and an
  empty keyword list. Note the mild wording tension: §7 and R37 say "no text",
  yet BUILD's schema requires a `text` string, and `CardFace.text` is documented
  as "The §8 cell this face implements, for the client and for test
  readability" — i.e. a description field, not literal printed rules text. I
  therefore described the statsOverride rule there rather than leaving it blank,
  since a blank would lose the only information §7 gives about this token. If
  you prefer strict fidelity to "no text", change both faces' `text` to `""`; no
  other field changes.

    4. **Sheep Token's "worth 2 Tributes" is text, not a keyword.** Confirmed
  three ways: it is not in §6.1's keyword table nor in the `Keyword` union in
  `catalog-types.ts`; §3.2's final-but-one bullet states it as a zone rule
  ("Sheep Tokens are worth 2 Tributes while on the field"); and §6.3's Tribute
  row makes it an engine detail of the *play validator* ("the Sheep Token counts
  as 2 toward that X while it is on the field"), with the carve-out I
  transcribed ("A tribute written into a card's script is an ordinary Sacrifice
  of the permanent that script names, where the Sheep Token's 2 never applies").
  Related plumbing already exists as `TargetDecl.amount` — "For Tribute: how
  many tributes the play costs (Sheep Tokens count 2, §6.3)" — so it belongs to
  the validator, not to the token's keyword set.

    5. **Rush Token keeps a plain `3/3` + `Rush`; I did not encode any stat
  override.** §7's token-rules bullet 1 is explicit that overrides are the
  summoning card's business: "Implement as the Rush Token definition plus a

    ## Rules I had to decide (SPEC silent) — proposed R-rows, highest existing
  row is R90

    1. **R91 A switch to the position a unit already holds does nothing.**
  `switchPosition(..., {to})` with `to` equal to the current position returns no
  error, emits no event and spends no exertion. Needed by
  `switchPositionOf({to})`/`switchAllPositions`; SPEC §4.1 only describes a
  flip.
    2. **R92 Only a unit on the field has a position.** `switchPosition` refuses
  a card dormant under a Stack or off the field with "that unit is not on the
  field", extending §3.2/R13 (which SPEC states for attacking only).
    3. **R93 A First Strike unit strikes once.** §4.3's mermaid literally shows
  the attacker striking in step 1 *and* step 2; the tests (and sanity) require
  step 2 to be only for whoever has not struck yet. The code implements "one
  strike each; First Strike moves it earlier".
    4. **R94 Both attack values are read once, at the start of the combat.**
  That is what makes the simultaneous step simultaneous (R59), and the First
  Strike survivor strikes back with its pre-combat attack.
    5. **R95 Cleave rides the attacker's single hit** (immediately after it,
  never the defender's strike-back), and a hero target cleaves nothing — there
  are no units adjacent to a hero. §4.4 step 10 + R63 give "belongs to the
  attack" but not the placement.
    6. **R96 A forced attack by a unit that is already gone is skipped
  silently** (no `attackDeclared`), and the sequence also stops once
  `state.result` is set. R53 spells out only "stops when the target is gone".
    7. **R5 addendum.** `LANE_RESTRICTED_ATTACKS` is read rather than
  hard-coded: if it is ever flipped to `true`, the target must stand in the
  attacker's own lane ("that target is not in this unit's lane"). SPEC defines
  no semantics for the flipped case, so this branch is a documented assumption
  and is dead today.
    8. **§4.2 step 4's trap window is a seam, not implemented here.**
  `declareAttack` spends the exertion *before* emitting `attackDeclared` (so a
  cancelled attack is still gone, per R44) and emits it before any damage, so My
  Pawn can fire off the event in M4. `combat.ts` deliberately does not call
  `traps.ts`/`triggers.ts`: someone must decide whether combat dispatches the
  window itself and checks for `attackCancelled`, or `reduce` interposes between
  validation and `resolveCombat`. No test pins it today.

    ## Integration finding: the server's port does not match what we built

    `apps/server/src/api/ports.ts` already declares a `LoadoutValidator` port.
  The composition root is meant to adapt us to it, so some translation is
  expected, but two differences are traps:

    - **`deck` is documented 0-based in the port and is 1-based here.** That is
  an off-by-one waiting to surface in the deckbuilder's error display. Pick one;
  I chose 1-based because it is the number the message itself prints.
    - **The port takes `catalogVersion` separately**, which reads as if the
  validator should compare it. We deliberately do not (see ambiguity 5). If the
  server assumed we would, stale catalogs go unchecked.
    - Lesser: port returns `LoadoutIssue[]` (empty means ok) vs our
  `LoadoutResult` union; `owned: ReadonlyMap` vs our `Record`; the port's
  `CatalogInfo` carries `isToken`/`isBanned` callbacks where we read the def and
  a `banned` list.

    ## SPEC §9.4 ambiguities — two implementers would differ, and what I chose

    1. **L5 is nearly unreachable on its own.** With `MAX_COPIES = 1`, two
  copies of a card means they are in one deck (L3) or two decks (L4), so the
  *plural* L5 message can never fire alone; L5 fires alone only in the `you own
  0` form. Real overlap in the rules, not a code defect. Test 14 pins it by
  asserting the rule set is exactly `["L3", "L5"]`. Worth revisiting if
  `MAX_COPIES` is ever raised.
    2. **All failures, not the first.** §9.4 does not say. I return every
  failure, because BUILD e2e/09 expects the builder to show each of L1–L6.
    3. **1-based `deck` field, absent on L1/L4/L5.** §9.4 says a failure "names
  the deck and the card" without saying whether that is the sentence or a field.
  L4's message names two decks while the field holds one, so L4 leaves it
  undefined — a client keying errors by deck cannot highlight either deck for L4
  without parsing the string.
    4. **An unknown or banned id still counts toward L2/L3/L4/L5** (only the
  token check is skipped, there being no def to read). So one typo'd id yields
  both an L6 and an L5 "you own 0". Deliberate, but a deckbuilder UX call you
  may want to revisit.
    5. **Catalog staleness is not a validator rule.** §9.4 mentions "stale
  catalog version is rejected at save and queue" in the same breath as L6; I
  left it to the endpoint per BUILD M6-T2 and check only membership in the
  snapshot handed in. Confirm the server actually does it — nothing here will.
    6. **L3's "no Token-tagged cards"** is literally about the tag, but I refuse
  `def.token || tags.includes("Token")`, mirroring the engine catalog's private
  `isToken`. Undecided by §9.4 if the two ever disagree.
    7. **Decks beyond the third** are still fully checked; §9.4 only says
  "exactly 3". A legal fourth deck yields L1 alone (pinned by a test).
    8. **An id both absent from the catalog and on the banned list** emits two
  L6 errors — missing and banned are independent checks. Arguably should be one.
    9. **An id absent from the collection is owned 0.** The sane reading, but
  §9.4 only says "the quantity owned".

    One change I made on my own judgement after the suite was written: L2
  pluralises its count, so a deck deleted down to one card reads `Deck 1 has 1
  card;` rather than `1 cards`. I added the test that pins it (27th test).

    Constants: `PROMPT_KINDS` (the ten kinds of §10.6, in spec order),
  `RESUME_HOOK` (`"resume"`), `MAX_PROMPT_ANSWERS` (256), `MAX_WORK_STEPS`

    - `openPrompt(sink, {player, kind, prompt, options, min?, max?, resume}) →
  PendingChoice | null` — one at a time (§10.1): returns null (and emits
  nothing) if a prompt is already open or there are no options, so the effect
  fizzles and the card still resolves. Id `q<nextId>` like `setup.ts`,

  re-enter any continuation (prompt answer, delayed effect, queued trigger,

  that hook/step is a no-op, not an error.
    - `applyResumable(sink, ctx, plan, effects, from?) → boolean` — the
  prompt-aware replacement for `resolve.applyEffects`.
    - `drainWork(sink) → boolean`, `runHookResumable(sink, instance, hookName,
  options?)` — drop-in for `resolve.runHook` on any path whose effects can ask
  something.

    ### How a continuation is represented (the previous failure)

    Two plain-JSON records, no closures anywhere:

    1. **`state.pending.resume`** (`state.Resume`): `{defId, hook, step,
  radiant, instanceId?, data}`. `hook` names a `Script` key — a step table
  (`resume: { picked: … }`, `step` picks the entry) or a hook of its own (`cry`,
  `delayed`; `step` then just labels the pause). Chaining is a step that opens
  the next prompt, so Private Tutor's three steps, Craft a Card's two Discovers
  and radiant Masochism Mask's two picks need no new machinery.
    2. **`state.work`** (the `WorkItem[]` the state owner just added, which
  `replay-scripted.test.ts` asserts is exercised): when a prompt opens *in the
  middle* of an effect list, `applyResumable` parks the **remainder** as a work
  item naming the same script/hook/step plus a control block in `resume.data`
  under one key `__paused = {from, targets, modes}` — the index to continue from
  and the selections the step was running with. `answerPrompt` runs the
  answered step and then drains `state.work` **newest-first** (each pause
  happened inside the previous one), stopping if a new prompt opens — the rest
  simply stays in state. So the tail is never restarted and never dropped, and a
  further prompt inside the tail nests correctly.

    Re-entry re-calls the hook (a pure builder, CLAUDE.md rule 5) and skips to
  `from`; holding the remaining `Effect[]` in state would be holding closures,
  which §9.3 forbids. The module deliberately runs **no** state check and
  dispatches **no** trigger — the §10.3/R59 loop calls in and keeps going.

  (`replay-scripted.test.ts:139`). Whoever owns script.ts should add these; tell
  me if that is me.

  No new field on `WorkItem` is needed, provided the three `Resume` fields are
  read as follows (this is exactly "what to run / which step / captured data /
  whose it is"):
  - `resume.hook` = the *sequence name*, i.e. the old `PendingWork["kind"]`:
  `"play" | "attack" | "deaths" | "reborn" | "endOfTurnHooks" | "turnEnd"` for
  engine sequences, or a card hook name for a card continuation. It is the
  handler key.
  - `resume.step` = which step of that sequence to pick up at (`"combo" | "cry"
  | "afterTraps" | "bury"` for the play pipeline).
  - `resume.data` = the captured payload (targets, modes, remaining instance
  ids, snapshots — all plain JSON).
  - `resume.defId`/`instanceId`/`radiant` = the card, when the sequence has one;
  `defId: ""` and no `instanceId` for a pure engine sequence (the precedent is
  `choose.ts`, which already emits `defId: ""` when `ctx.self` is null).

  THE API (`packages/engine/src/work.ts`), for the playSteps/reduce agent and
  the prompts agent:

  ```ts
  export type WorkHandler = (sink: EngineSink, item: WorkItem) => void;
  export function registerWorkHandler(hook: string, handler: WorkHandler): void;
  // module scope, like registerScripts
  export function owe(sink: EngineSink, ...resumes: Resume[]): WorkItem[];
  // append, FIFO; = pushWork
  export function pushWork(sink: EngineSink, resume: Resume, owner?: PlayerId):
  WorkItem;
  export function hasWork(state: GameState): boolean;
  export function peekWork(state: GameState): WorkItem | undefined;
  export function takeWork(state: GameState): WorkItem | undefined;
  // shift
  export function dropWork(state: GameState, match: (item: WorkItem) =>
  boolean): WorkItem[];
  export function runWorkItem(sink: EngineSink, item: WorkItem): void;
  // throws on an unregistered hook
  export function runNextWork(sink: EngineSink): boolean;
  // take + run one; false when empty
  export function runWork(sink: EngineSink): void;
  // drain until empty or paused
  export function paused(sink: EngineSink): boolean;
  // pending !== null || result !== null
  ```

  Usage, so the three of us agree:
  - A sequence that is about to stop calls `if (paused(sink)) { owe(sink, {
  hook: "play", step: "cry", … }); return; }` — the remainder, never a closure.
  - `settle` (triggers.ts) drains work *before* popping the trigger queue: `if
  (runNextWork(sink)) { continue; }`, and only returns when `dispatch` and
  `work` are both empty. The interrupted sequence's own remainder comes before
  anything new.
  - `prompts.ts` keeps `answerPrompt`/`resumeScript`/`resumeAt`/`resumeSelf` and
  runs the answered card step *inline* (not through the queue); `reduce` then
  calls `settle`, which drains the owed remainder. Nesting therefore needs no
  stack: FIFO plus inline answers gives inner-before-outer ordering.
  - `owner` defaults to `state.active`; ids are `w<nextId>` and `seq` comes from
  `nextSeq`, so the queue replays identically.

  I am writing work.ts now against your WorkItem; I will write
  `test/pauses.test.ts` with string steps. If fix (1) is not in when I
  typecheck, my test will show that one error and nothing else.

    ### One finding that needed a decision the spec does not make (please add a
  §11 R-row — I was told not to edit other files)

    **`PlayerView.events` is typed `GameEvent[]`, and `GameEvent` carries hidden
  information.** `drawn`, `addedToHand`, `shuffledIn` and `bounced` name a card
  *with its `defId`* on its way into a hand or library; `costChanged` names an
  instance discounted **in hand**. Without filtering, the M3-T6 acceptance
  criterion fails outright: after one `endTurn` the stream holds p2's
  `drawn`/`addedToHand` events whose `defId` is a card still in p2's hand.

    I could not drop the fields (they are non-optional on the union) and did not
  want to drop the events (each has a row in §10.10's animation table), so
  `redactEvent` keeps each event's shape and cue and replaces the identity with
  `HIDDEN_ID`, decided per event by **where the card sits now** (`mayRead`):
  library → never; hand → owner only; backrow → `backrowIsPublic`; everything
  else public. That is history-correct — a card drawn last turn and played this
  turn is public again; a unit bounced into the opponent's hand stops being
  readable the moment it lands. `shuffledIn.position` is blanked for **both**
  players, since §9.1 lists "library order" as hidden without qualifying by
  player. The switch is exhaustive over all 40 event types on purpose, so a new
  event type (§10.3) cannot be added without a decision at the boundary. **This
  rule and the `HIDDEN_ID` sentinel are the part §10.8 does not cover and should
  become an R-row with a named test.**

    ### Other gaps in `packages/shared/src/view.ts` (real findings, none
  blocking)

    1. **`BackrowView`'s visible branch has no `owner`/`controller`, though
  `UnitView` has both.** After a steal/board swap/rotation a trap p2 controls

    3. **No `reserved` alongside `locks`.** §3.2/R64: a zone held for a dying

    4. **`HeroView.power` has no `instanceId`**, so the client cannot build

    5. **`PendingView`'s `{forYou:false, pendingFor}` withholds `kind`, but the

    ## `traps.ts` API

    `isTrapType(state, instance)`, `isFieldTrap`, `TRAP_WINDOW_EVENTS`
  (`["turnEnded"]`), `isTrapWindowEvent(event)`, `trapsInOrder(state)` (R68:
  active side's backrow lanes 1–5, then the opponent's), `trapsWatching(state,
  event) → TrapMatch[]`, `fireTrap(sink, match, event) → boolean`,
  `fireTrapsFor(sink, event) → TrapDispatch` (immediate response path; withholds

  `TrapDispatch { fired: string[]; paused: boolean }`.

    `fireTrap` = emit `trapFired` → run every woken trigger → `consumeTrap` →
  `stateCheck`, so a trap resolves to completion (forced attacks included)
  before the interrupted action continues. A prompt opened by a trap leaves
  `paused: true` and stops the dispatch; a Trap goes to its **owner's**
  graveyard with an `enteredGraveyard` event, a Field Trap stays and is `faceUp`
  for ever (R33). Consumption is unconditional on the effect achieving anything
  (R17 Immutable Sheepish, R61 no-legal-target).

    ## Rules I had to decide (SPEC silent) — proposed R-rows

    1. **A trap needs a predicate, not an empty effect list, to stay armed.**
  R61 fixes `run() → []` as "fired, consumed, did nothing", so a trap whose
  *condition* failed cannot signal that through `run`. Bear Honeypot ("costing 1
  or less"), My Pawn ("would be lethal") and Unlicensed Experimentation ("the
  opponent … whose type matches one you control") would all be spent by an event
  they should ignore. I read an optional `when?: (ctx & {event}) => boolean`
  off each `TriggerDef` structurally (absent ⇒ the `on` match alone arms the
  trap) — **`script.ts` must add `when?` to `TriggerDef`** and the trap cards
  must use it. Two existing fixtures disagree under the default: `rulings-b`'s
  `empty-trap` needs `[]` ⇒ consumed, `rulings-a`'s `sheepish` puts "not my own
  summon" inside `run` and needs to stay armed. Proposed row: *"R97 A trap's
  condition — a trap fires when its trigger's `on` matches the event and its
  `when` predicate admits it; with the predicate satisfied, an empty effect list
  still spends the trap (R61). A trap with no predicate answers every event it
  names, on either side."* Test name `it("R97 …")`.
    2. **The end-of-turn window owns `turnEnded`.** Nothing says the immediate
  dispatch must skip it; if it does not, a `turnEnded`-watching Field Trap fires
  twice (once as a response, once in the window) and R62's expected log
  `["end","trap:p1","trap:p2","delayed"]` becomes four entries.
  `TRAP_WINDOW_EVENTS` withholds it. Proposed row: *"R98 The trap window's
  events are its alone — an event the §2.2 trap window is scheduled to deliver
  is not offered to the immediate trap check, so a window trap fires once per
  turn end."*
    3. **Default `side` for a declaration.** `TargetFilter.side` is optional and
  §10.6 never states a default. I use "any" for every kind (which is what the
  bare-`target` test asserts), except `tribute` → "ally" (§6.3 "sacrifice X of
  *your* units"); a `hand` pick is forced to the chooser whatever it says
  (§9.1), which the test pins.
    4. **A hero passes no `type`/`tags` filter.** A hero has neither, so a
  filter naming either cannot reach one; `notTags` alone still admits it.
    5. **The card being played is never offered out of the hand it is leaving**,
  even without `excludeSelf` (the test asserts this).
    6. **Tribute exactness and payability.** A Tribute set must meet the cost
  *and* be minimal (no unit could be dropped and still pay), because the Sheep
  Token's 2 makes overshoot unavoidable but wasted sacrifices are not "sacrifice
  X". Unlike a target, an unpayable Tribute **refuses** the play (`"<name>
  needs Tribute N"`, BUILD #66 "play refused without a tribute"). `#55 Lava
  Golem`'s "may tribute enemy units" has no flag: I read
  `staticFlags.tributeEnemies` structurally — **`script.ts` must add
  `tributeEnemies?: boolean` beside `tribute`.** Proposed row: *"R99 Paying a
  Tribute — the tributed set must meet the printed X and be minimal, the Sheep
  Token counting 2 (§3.2); a board that cannot reach X makes the play illegal,
  and only a card that says so may tribute enemy units."*
    7. **Non-final declarations take a fixed count.** R90 says the last takes
  the remainder; I make every earlier one take exactly `min(decl.min,
  offeredCount)` — clamped by what the board offers, so an unsatisfiable
  declaration takes none and the next still reads its own slot (this is what
  makes "a declaration the board cannot satisfy does not refuse the play" work
  with several declarations).
    8. **A zone lane out of range** is refused explicitly (`"there is no units
  zone 9"`); `zones.isOpen` reports an out-of-range lane as open, which
  `reduce.ts` currently trusts.

    ## 1. `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine/src/s
  ubsystems/fuse.ts`

    Exports:
    - `fuse(sink: EngineSink, args: FuseArgs): CardInstance | null` — the whole
  verb.
    - `type FuseArgs = { ingredients: readonly CardInstance[]; target?:
  CardInstance; toHand?: PlayerId }`
    - `FUSE_MIN_INGREDIENTS = 2`, `CRAFTED_CARD_COST = 0`

    Behaviour per R77 / §6.3 / BUILD M3-T7: builds a `t-<n>` def into
  `state.transientDefs` (id derived from the transientDefs count, so replay
  regenerates it), base form from the ingredients' base forms and radiant form
  from their radiant forms (stats summed, keywords deduped by `keywordKey`, tags
  unioned, texts joined), `cost = min(Σ printedCost, FUSE_COST_CAP)`, type =
  target's else shared else first, promoted to `Field Trap` when the result is a
  trap type and any ingredient is a Field Trap. With a target on the field it
  keeps that instance (only `defId`, summed buffs and united `grantedKeywords`
  change; damage/exertion/zone/position/summonedTurn/counters/memory/radiant/`st
  atsOverride`/vanilla untouched) and the other ingredients cease to exist via
  `removeFromAnyZone` + `zone = {z:"gone"}` — no graveyard, no Death,
  `counters.destroyed` untouched. Returns `null` (state untouched) for <2
  ingredients, an Immutable target (R23/R61), a target not on the field, or
  neither `target` nor `toHand`. Emits the existing `fused` event.

    **How a fused trap's two trigger conditions are represented:** the
  ingredients' `script.triggers` arrays are *concatenated*, each entry keeping
  its own `on` list, its own `run` and its own `when` predicate (traps.ts's
  `TrapTrigger` extra field survives the spread). `traps.fireTrap` already
  filters by `when` and runs only the armed entries, so "every ingredient's
  condition, only the fired script runs" falls out. Ids are namespaced
  `"<ingredientDefId>:<id>"` so two ingredients with a `"turn-end"` trigger stay
  two conditions (trigger ids double as resume `hook` names in `triggers.ts`).

    Script concatenation is generic over `Script`'s shape (so it survives the
  type growing): functions → one hook returning the concatenation, arrays →
  concatenated, nested objects (`staticFlags`, `resume`) → combined key-by-key,
  booleans → OR, numbers → max. `cost` is dropped (R77's capped sum must win
  over a Ceaseless Void hook) and `setStat` is summed; both are called out as
  the only non-list-returning members.

    Registration: the fused `CardScripts` pair joins the module-level script
  registry (`registerScripts({...registeredScripts(), [def.id]: …})`), because
  scripts are code and `GameState` is JSON-only. The def itself is state.
  Deterministic id ⇒ replay-safe.

    ## 2. `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine/src/s
  ubsystems/heroPower.ts`

    Exports: `HeroPower`/`HeroPowerName` types, `HERO_POWERS` (7 rows in §8
  order, with `x`, `label`, `radiantLabel`, `build`), `HERO_POWER_NAMES`,
  `powerByName`, `powerOf`, `powerCostOf`, `ensurePower`, `usedThisTurn`,
  `rollPower()` (Effect), `usePower()` (Effect), `heroPower` (Hook),
  `whyCannotActivate`, `activatePower`, plus `POWER_KEY="power"`,
  `POWER_USED_KEY="usedTurn"`, `POWER_RESUME="heroPower"`, `POWER_DATA_KEY`,
  `POWER_HEALTH_COST=2`, `RUSH_TOKEN_INDEX="T-rush"`,
  `FELINOR_TOKEN_INDEX="T-felinor"`.

    Powers: `recruit`(3), `draw`(1), `ping`(1), `burn`(1), `rush`(2),
  `felinor`(1), `discover`(2), with the radiant variants of §8 #98. Cost flows
  through the ordinary pipeline: #98's `cost` hook is `powerCostOf`, which
  `printedCost` reads ahead of the printed `"X"`, so nothing special-cases the
  card. The memory keys and the stored *name* string match what the landed
  `viewFor.heroPowerView` already reads.

    **How a power's prompt is resumed:** having read the landed `prompts.ts`, a
  prompt's `Resume` carries `hook: RESUME_HOOK ("resume")` and `step: <name>`,
  and `hookFor` looks the answer up in the card's `Script.resume` table. So
  `ping`/`discover` open their prompt with `step: POWER_RESUME` (through
  `effects/choose`'s `chooseTarget` / `discoverFromCatalog`, so this file never
  imports `prompts.ts`), and #98 wires it in one line: `resume: {
  [POWER_RESUME]: heroPower }`. Each power's builder is written so it *is* its
  own continuation: with a selection in `ctx.targets` it acts, without one it
  opens the prompt — so `heroPower(ctx)` just re-runs the builder. `usePower`
  marks `memory.usedTurn` **before** running effects, so a paused activation
  cannot buy a second use. No power has an effect after the prompt-opening one,
  so `applyEffects` is safe; that constraint is documented.

    ## Env-var contract

    **Public** (`VITE_` prefix, shipped to the browser, safe because RLS is the
  access control): `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
  (`sb_publishable_…`), `VITE_SERVER_HTTP_URL`, `VITE_SERVER_WS_URL`,
  `VITE_CATALOG_VERSION`.

    **Server-only** (never in a bundle, never in git): `SUPABASE_URL`,
  `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` (`sb_secret_…`, bypasses every RLS policy),
  `DATABASE_URL` (the transactions the Data API cannot express),
  `SUPABASE_JWKS_URL` (optional, defaults to
  `${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`), `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`
  (legacy HS256, discouraged), `CODE_PEPPER` (≥32 chars, HMAC pepper — so the
  pepper never reaches Postgres and a DB dump yields no redeemable code),
  `PORT`, `PUBLIC_ORIGINS`, `NODE_ENV`, `CATALOG_VERSION`, `E2E`. `env.ts`
  reports every missing variable in one error naming where to get each, and
  never logs a secret. R79's values are deliberately **not** env vars — they are
  gameplay, so they are named exports in `config.ts` per BUILD §2.

    ## SPEC clauses I could not satisfy without a decision → R-rows to add
  (existing rows end at R90)

    Each is marked `-- NOT IN SPEC:` / `// NOT IN SPEC:` in the source and
  tabulated in `docs/architecture.md` §11.

    | # | Topic | Decision |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | R91 | The code alphabet as a literal | `23456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ`.
  **SPEC's "32-symbol alphabet without 0/O/1/I/l" is unsatisfiable as written**
  — dropping `0`,`1`,`I`,`O`,`L` from 36 alphanumerics leaves 31.
  Uppercase-only and dropping `0`,`1`,`I`,`O` gives exactly 32, so 16 chars are
  exactly 80 bits and a 6-char room code is 30. Lowercase `l` is excluded by
  normalising to upper case. |
    | R92 | Catalog version format | A short opaque string on every `cards` row,
  mirrored in `app.settings`; `core-1` for Core. SPEC requires a version and a
  rejection but never says what one looks like. |
    | R93 | Circuit-breaker threshold/window | 100 system-wide failures in 600
  s. SPEC requires "a threshold in a window" and names neither. |
    | R94 | Constant-time failure floor | Responses padded to 250 ms. SPEC
  requires "identical time"; M6-T1 tests within 5 ms over 50 samples; SQL alone
  cannot deliver it, so the floor is a server responsibility. |
    | R95 | Sweeper and reaper cadence | Sweep every 3 s ("every few seconds");
  reaper every 30 s. |
    | R96 | Action-flooding limits | 5 actions/s per match, 300 req/min per
  account. §9.8 requires both and names no numbers. |
    | R97 | Room-code reuse | Unique among matches that are not `over`, so codes
  recycle. |
    | R98 | Launch grant quantity | One copy of every non-token card, granted by
  a trigger on `pending → active`, idempotent. |
    | R99 | A match the reaper resolves | The reaper finishes stuck matches
  itself rather than flagging them for a server that may be the crashed
  component. Consequence: a reaper-resolved ceiling draw records `turns = 0` and
  leaves ratings unchanged, where an actor-resolved draw applies the real Elo.
  |

    Also worth a SPEC sentence, not an R-row: §9.2's "API functions" and "Match
  actor" are two responsibilities of one Node process here. Supabase has no
  Durable-Object equivalent — Edge Functions are request-scoped isolates with no
  durable identity, no surviving timer and no way to hold two WebSockets — so
  the actor is the one piece Supabase cannot supply. `docs/architecture.md` §4
  argues this from §9.2 and ARCHITECTURE-CCG §2.1, takes the "long-running
  process" option, and costs out each downside against the SPEC mitigation that
  already covers it. The actor is written behind a four-method interface (`now`,
  `setAlarm`, `appendAction`, `send`) so a Durable Object port is a
  reimplementation of four methods.

    ### Ordering and where the state check runs

    One pass of `settle`: **dispatch every undispatched event → return if paused
  → drain `state.work` → `stateCheck` → (re-dispatch if the check emitted) →
  pop one entry → apply it whole.** So the check sits between whole
  effects/triggers and never splits one (R59), and a check runs after each
  queued trigger before the next pops.

    Dispatch of one event = §10.3 steps C then D: `traps.fireTrapsFor(sink,
  event)` fires traps immediately and to completion (traps are **not** queued —
  that is what "a trap fires before a queued trigger" means), then every
  non-trap holder's matching trigger is appended in R68 order: active side
  first, then the opponent; per side unit lanes 1–5, backrow 1–5, hand,
  graveyard. Across events the queue is FIFO in emission order. `turnEnded` is
  passed over for traps (R62's scheduled window is `turn.ts`'s
  `traps.runTrapWindow`). Delayed effects are not queued here at all — they stay
  at their R62 point via `modifiers.dueDelayed`.

    `dispatched` is a monotonic cursor on the sink that only ever advances by
  what it consumed, so a mid-action `settle` followed by more emissions loses
  nothing — the M3 review's **B-2** cannot recur (probe 2/4).

    ### Prompts (B-3 closed without a new state field)

    Queueing is pure and cannot pause, so it is flushed **before** the pending
  check: every event emitted so far is already in `state.triggerQueue` (with its
  event) when an action returns paused. `settle` then returns on `state.pending
  !== null`; the `answer` action calls `prompts.answerPrompt` (which runs the
  resume + `drainWork`) and then `settle` again, and the queue picks up where it
  left off. A trigger's effect list is applied with `prompts.applyResumable`,
  so a prompt stops the list instead of being stepped over. A trap dispatch a
  prompt interrupts is parked as one front-of-queue `OWED_TO_TRAPS` entry naming
  the traps that still have to see the event, so it resumes without re-firing a
  Field Trap. Verified by probe (scratchpad
  `.../scratchpad/triggers/probe.mts`, 8 probes, all pass), including a JSON
  round-trip of the paused state between pause and answer.

⏺ I've found the real shape of this bug, and it's subtler than either agent's
  proposal — neither pure LIFO nor pure FIFO is correct. Let me verify my
  reasoning against the pipeline before ruling.

  Scenario: a Cry's effect list [damage, chooseTarget, damage] pauses inside
  play step 5.
  - The Cry parks its tail (W1), then the pipeline parks steps 6–8 (W2). Push
    order W1, W2 — and W1 must run first, since step 6 follows step 5. FIFO wins
    here; LIFO would run step 6 before the Cry finished.
  - Now resume W1, and it opens a second prompt, parking W3. Queue is [W2, W3].
    W3 is still inside step 5, so it must precede W2. LIFO wins here; FIFO would
    run step 6 too early.

  So the correct rule is: within one pause cascade, innermost-first; a new
  cascade goes ahead of everything already owed. That needs one integer of
  state.

    ## 1. The M2 gate — the seed and the exact cause

    The invariant that actually broke was invariant 3's last clause, not
  literally "negative health": no hero or unit was ever left at negative health,
  and no dead unit was left on the field. The breach was **`damage event with a
  non-positive amount`**, in **12 of the 1,000 cases** (the test's break-at-5
  hid the rest; I widened it temporarily to enumerate them, then restored it).
  Seeds: **`m2-combat-2`** (first), then 12, 245, 344, 357, 474, 571, 690, 801,
  879, 966.

    **Cause — §4.4 step 5's Trample cap, in `packages/engine/src/damage.ts`.**
  The cap read `dealt = Math.max(0, view.health)`. When the target unit is
  *already* at 0 or less health, that makes `dealt` 0 and `trampleExcess` the
  whole amount, but the code still ran `damage += 0`, set `lastDamagedBy`,
  emitted `{type:"damage", amount:0}` and ran steps 6–8 on it. R63 and §4.4's
  zero rule both say a hit that is 0 emits no `damage` event and triggers
  nothing.

    `m2-combat-2` concretely: p1 `c41` is a radiant Trampler (12/8) with granted
  Poisonous; p2 `c42` is a Rusher whose generator dressing dragged its max
  health to 0 (`buffs.health -= maxHealth`), so it stood at 0/0 when the attack
  was declared. The strike is 12, the Trample cap clamps it to the defender's
  health of 0 → `amount: 0` event on `c42`, plus 11 to hero p2 (12 less p2's
  hero armor 1). `m2-combat-344` is the same path on the *defender's*
  strike-back (a radiant Trample+Lifesteal defender hitting a Cleaver whose max
  health had been dragged to 0), which also let Lifesteal heal off a hit that
  dealt nothing.

    **Fix:** when the Trample cap leaves 0 for the unit, nothing is dealt — no
  event, no `lastDamagedBy`, no steps 6–8 — and step 9 still carries the whole
  amount to the target's controller's hero, so R63's "Lifesteal heals the total
  once" still holds (the heal now comes entirely off the Trample instance).

    Cleave and R95 were already correct: `cleave()` is called only from the
  attacker's `strike()`, never from `strikeBack`, and returns early on a hero
  target. R69 was correct in both `stateCheck.isDying` and `combat.hasFallen`.

    ## Root cause of the Cry double-fire (one sentence)

    `drive` in `playSteps.ts` parked the pipeline's own continuation on
  `state.work` *before* running any step, and step 4 (`placeStep`) ends in
  `settle(sink)` — which drains `state.work` before it pops a trigger — so the
  play's own nested `settle` took that item and ran steps 5–8 (the Cry, Echo,
  the Spell's graveyard move) and then handed control back to `drive`'s loop,
  which ran step 5 onwards a second time.

    Fix: the pipeline now owes its remainder **only at the moment a step
  actually pauses**, so there is exactly one owner per step — the driver while
  it is on the stack, `state.work` once it has stopped. It also fixes R113's
  order as a side effect: `work.ts` parks at `state.workCursor`, which the
  pausing scope has just advanced past its own item, so a Cry's parked tail now
  lands *ahead* of steps 6–8 (they come after the Cry, not inside it), where
  pre-parking put the pipeline ahead of the tail.

    ### The one test I judged wrong: `triggers.test.ts` "§10.3 pauses the
  opponent's action until the trap's prompt is answered"

    It asserted `notes(answered)).toEqual(["answered"])`, i.e. that the played
  card's Cry never fires. p1 plays `crier` (Cry → note "cry"); p2's `askTrap`
  answers the `summoned` of step 4 and prompts, so the play pauses between step
  4 and step 5. Once p2 answers, the trap has resolved to completion and "the
  opponent's action continues" (§10.3), so step 5 runs and the Cry fires — R1
  ("a play from hand fires Cry, exactly once") and R113 ("a work item that
  cannot be resumed is a lost sequence … must never be dropped"). R17's "Cry
  lost" is specifically Sheepish *removing the card* (`stillResolving` → null),
  which is not this fixture. Nothing in SPEC or BUILD M3-T2 (acceptance: "pauses
  the opponent's action until answered") asks for the Cry to be dropped.

    I strengthened it rather than weakened it: it now asserts
  `notes(paused)).toEqual([])` (the trap really does go before the Cry),
  `notes(answered)).toEqual(["answered", "cry"])` (trap first, then the play
  resumes — once) and `answered.work).toEqual([])` (nothing left owed).

    ## Blocked: R70's cast Echo

    `echo.test.ts`'s R70 test calls `resolve.castCard` directly, and `castCard`
  runs `runHook(sink, instance, "cry", options)` and then moves a Spell to the
  graveyard itself — it never reaches §10.5 step 6, so no `echoNextSpell` grant
  is consumed and no repeat happens. There is no hook I can reach from
  `playSteps.ts`: nothing parks work for a cast and the trigger registry only
  queries card scripts. **Per your instruction I did not touch `resolve.ts`.**
  Recommended change, untested by me:

    In `playSteps.ts` (my file — say the word and I'll add it):
    ```ts
    export function runCastSteps(
      sink: EngineSink,
      instance: CardInstance,
      options: { controller?: PlayerId; targets?: readonly Selection[]; modes?:
  readonly string[] } = {},
    ): void {
      drive(sink, {
        instanceId: instance.id, defId: instance.defId,
        player: options.controller ?? instance.controller,
        costPaid: 0, zone: null,
        targets: [...(options.targets ?? [])], modes: [...(options.modes ??
  [])], tributes: [],
        at: PLAY_STEPS.indexOf("resolve"),
        hookAt: 0, resolveAt: 0, echoQueued: false, repeat: null, awaiting:
  null,
      });
    }
    ```
    In `resolve.ts`'s `castCard`, replace `runHook(sink, instance, "cry",
  options)` **and** the `if (def.type === "Spell") { moveToZone… }` block with
  `runCastSteps(sink, instance, options)`. Two caveats for whoever lands it: (a)
  it creates an import cycle `resolve → playSteps → resolve` (harmless in ESM —
  only hoisted function declarations are called at runtime, and no lint rule
  bans cycles here — but the clean alternative is to move step 6 into its own
  `src/echo.ts` that both import); (b) step 7 moves *any* card still in
  `resolving` to the graveyard, so a cast **permanent** would now be graveyarded
  instead of being left in `resolving` as `castCard` leaves it today —
  `castCard` should place a cast permanent on the field (step 4's job) before
  handing over. The step 6 machinery itself is already proven by the four
  passing echo tests (repeats, fresh prompts per repeat, prompts pausing the
  repeats behind them, `echoQueue` surviving a JSON round trip).

    ## Ruling that wants an R-row (wording proposed, number not picked — §11
  ends at R113)

    **Who owns a paused sequence's remaining steps.** "An engine sequence owes
  its remainder to `state.work` only at the moment it pauses, never in advance:
  while its driver is on the stack those steps are the driver's alone, so a
  resolution loop that runs *inside* one of them — §10.5 step 4's own `settle`,
  which drains work before it pops a trigger — can neither take nor run the

    ## Rulings I need R-rows for (wording proposed; I edited neither SPEC nor
  picked numbers)

    1. **Who continues an interrupted sequence.** R113 says what order work
  resumes in but not who drains it, and the answer is load-bearing for anyone
  driving the engine outside `reduce`. Proposed: *"Answering a prompt continues
  what it interrupted. `answer` re-enters the step its `resume` names and then
  drains `state.work` in R113's order, stopping at the next prompt, which parks
  its own tail. The state check and the trigger queue stay with the resolution
  loop, which drains again and finds nothing owed, so a sequence is finished by
  the action that answered it and not by whatever runs next."*
    2. **How a declared `tribute` pick travels.** R81 says "a declared `hand` or
  `zone` pick travels in `targets`" and lists Tribute separately, so nothing
  states what the engine actually requires: a `tribute` declaration's chosen
  units travel in `targets` (that is where the script reads them, #22), while
  its `amount` — when present — is §6.3's Tribute *cost*, paid from
  `play.tributes` and refusing the play when the board cannot pay it (#66). A
  card with both therefore names its units twice, once as the cost and once as
  the pick. Proposed: *"A `tribute` declaration is two things at once. Its
  chosen permanents travel in `targets`, like every other declared pick, which
  is where the script reads them (#22). Its `amount`, when it has one, is §6.3's
  Tribute cost, which travels in `play.tributes`, counts a Sheep Token 2 and
  refuses the play when the board cannot pay it — so a card that declares both
  names its units in both lists, and `legalActions` enumerates them that way."*
    3. **Minor, for your eye only:** §10.1's `GameState` listing has no
  `work`/`workCursor` rows, though R113 names `state.work` and `state.ts`
  declares both with R113 in the doc comment. Worth adding two lines to §10.1 so
  the state model is complete.

    ## Gaps found in scripts / engine (none of which I touched)

    1. **`heroArmor` — the whole of #84.** As above. Highest-value item: ten
  failing tests collapse to it.
    2. **#85 is not wired to `fuseCards`.** The verb now exists as `fuseCards({
  defIds?, instanceIds?, targetInstanceId?, toHand? })`
  (`packages/engine/src/effects/fuse.ts`), so #85's long "ENGINE GAP 2 — NO FUSE
  VERB" header is **stale**. Note the shape differs from what that header asked
  for: there is no `pick: "random" | "all"`, so the card must do the draw
  itself with `ctx.rng.pick` in `run` (legal — `ctx.rng` is on `EffectContext`
  and §9.3/R60 determinism holds) and emit one `fuseCards({ instanceIds:
  [played.id], targetInstanceId: chosen })` per target.
    3. **`effects/fuse.ts` defeats radiant #85's "one fusion at a time".**
  `subsystems/fuse.ts` explicitly supports it ("an ingredient that already
  ceased to exist in an earlier fusion still fuses… which is what lets radiant
  #85 fuse the played permanent onto each matching permanent separately"), but
  the wrapper resolves `instanceIds` with `findInstance` and drops what it
  cannot find, citing R86. After the first fusion the played card is
  `{z:"gone"}` and unreachable, so the second call sees `ingredients.length` 1 <
  `FUSE_MIN_INGREDIENTS` 2 and returns `null`. Radiant #85 therefore cannot
  fuse twice through the wrapper as written. Either the wrapper should keep a
  gone ingredient when it was named explicitly, or #85 must pass the played card
  as `defIds: [played.defId]` for fusions 2..n. My radiant "onto every such
  permanent" test will stay red until one of those happens.
    4. **#39's header is stale in two places**, both now harmless but misleading
  to the next reader: (a) `addToHand` already accepts `costMod`
  (`effects/addToHand.ts`), so the "MISSING VERB ARGUMENT" note is obsolete; (b)
  the claim that "`reduce.ts` moves a resolving Spell to the graveyard
  unconditionally after its Cry, which drags this card straight back out of
  exile" is wrong — `playSteps.finishStep` moves the card only `if (card.zone.z
  === "resolving")`, so "exile this on play" survives. My exile tests pass.
    5. **`turn.runDelayed` still cannot re-enter a `resume` step table.** It
  calls `runHook(sink, card, effect.resume.hook as HookName)`, and
  `resolve.hookOf` does `script[name]` and *calls* it, so only a `Hook` on
  `script.delayed` is reachable; `"resume"` would fetch the step-table object
  and throw. `effects/delay.ts` works around this by defaulting `hook` to
  `DELAYED_HOOK = "delayed"`, and #39 now registers its step under **both**
  `delayed` and `resume`. Worth fixing centrally (route through
  `prompts.runResume` when `hook === RESUME_HOOK`) so cards stop registering the
  same hook twice; `packages/engine/test/effects-delay.test.ts` already notes
  it.
    6. **Harness sharp edge (not a bug, but it bit me).** `FieldEntry.faceUp:
  false` is not written to the instance — `placeOne` sets it only when `true` —
  so a face-down trap reads `faceUp === undefined`, not `false`.
  `packages/cards/test/060-bear-honeypot.test.ts:70` asserts `toBe(false)` and
  fails on that alone. I assert `.not.toBe(true)`. Either the harness should
  write the flag or the README should say the field is tri-state.
    7. **§2.5 auto-end cascade.** Playing an embiggened #84 for all 4 mana
  leaves a hand whose only card is unaffordable, and the turn auto-ends
  *immediately*, so a following `endTurn()` lands on the wrong player ("it is
  not your turn"). I gave p1 a body (#7) so a `switchPosition` keeps the turn
  meaningful. The README warns about empty hands but not about a hand that is
  merely unaffordable — worth a sentence.

    # Gaps found

    ## 1. ENGINE — the `Stack` keyword is not implemented anywhere (blocks 5
  tests, #92)
    `grep -rn '"Stack"' packages/engine/src` returns **nothing**. Two specific
  places:
    - `packages/engine/src/playChoices.ts`, `refuseZone`: `if (!isOpen(state,
  {…})) return "that ${row} zone is not open"` — refuses an occupied zone
  unconditionally. `legalZonesFor` (same file, "every empty, unlocked,
  unreserved zone of the right row") likewise never offers an occupied lane, so
  `legalActions` won't offer the play either.
    - `packages/engine/src/playSteps.ts`, `placeStep`: `placeOnField(state,
  card, run.zone)` — never passes `{ stack: true }`.

    Everything else is already in place: `zones.placeOnField(…, { stack })`
  builds the pile and `removeFromField` resumes the card beneath;
  `activeUnitsOf`/`dormantUnitsOf` exist; `combat.switchPosition` already
  refuses a dormant card via `isActiveOnField` (R92); `triggerHolderFor` already
  registers nothing for a dormant card (R13); `legalSelectionsFor` already
  offers only the top of a pile; `viewFor` already reports `buried`. So the fix
  is: let `refuseZone`/`legalZonesFor` accept an occupied (unlocked, unreserved)
  **unit** zone when `unitView(card).keywords` (or `faceOf`) has `Stack`, and
  pass `{ stack: true }` from `placeStep`. #92's `setStat` hook itself is
  correct and already proven on 15 passing tests.

  blocker is stale

  `effects/draw.ts`. `draw({count})` only takes the top; `addToHand({defId})`

    # Rulings SPEC does not make (proposed wording; I edited neither SPEC.md nor
  picked R-numbers — §11 is at R113)

    1. **#92 self-exclusion under Fuse.** R77 unions an ingredient's tags, so a
  fused Felinor Fiender can carry the `Felinor` tag and would otherwise feed its
  own layer 2. The script excludes itself by instance id; SPEC does not rule.
  Proposed: *"Felinor Fiender never counts itself, even when Fuse (R77) has
  given it the Felinor tag: 'all your Felinors' means every other Felinor you
  control."*

  if that tag is corrected to `Felinor` (see below) two Fienders would each read
  the other. Proposed: *"Layer 2 reads each Felinor's layer-4 stats, so a
  second Felinor Fiender contributes only its printed and buffed stats and never
  its own layer-2 total; the layer never recurses."*
    3. **#92 / R39's floor — per stat, per Felinor, or on the total?** The
  script floors the *combined* attack and the *combined* max health separately.
  SPEC's R39 says only "never below printed". Proposed: *"The
  never-below-printed floor applies to the combined total of each stat
  separately — not per Felinor, and not to the pair together."* (Unreachable
  today: only auras subtract stats, and layer 2 reads layer 4, so no Core card
  can hand a Felinor a negative permanent buff. I said so in the file rather
  than asserting it.)
    4. **#93 grade E and a card played twice in one turn.** R86 says a card that
  merely moved zone stays in the pool, but `turnLog.playedIds` holds one entry
  per *play*, so a card played, bounced and replayed is weighted double in the
  random pick. Proposed: *"A card that appears more than once in a turn's play
  log is one entry in grade E's pool."*
    5. **#93's grade across a control change.** #87 Pocket Chaos's board swap,
  #36 radiant and #49 can move a Combo-Index to the other side. The counter
  travels with the instance, so the threshold would then be read against the
  *new* controller's turn log. SPEC does not rule. Proposed: *"Combo-Index's
  grade counter stays on the instance through a change of control, and its
  end-of-turn check reads its current controller's turn log."*
    6. **#94's exile order within the three zones.** §8 lists "library, hand and
  GY" but does not say whether the exile is one simultaneous batch or
  sequential per zone — which matters for R55's counters and for anything
  reacting to an exile. Proposed: *"Genn's Greed exiles in the order §8 names —
  library, then hand, then graveyard — each card its own exile."*

    ## 1. The window fix (`packages/engine/src/traps.ts`)

    **How the parked window is represented.** One work item, parked through
  `work.owe` at the moment of the pause and never before it (R117):

    ```
    resume = { defId: "", hook: TRAP_WINDOW_WORK /* "@trapWindow" */, step:
  "window",
               radiant: false, data: { event, owed: string[] } }
    ```

    `data.event` is the `turnEnded` event the window is delivering; `data.owed`
  is the instance ids of the traps that have **not** been offered it, in the
  order the window had. All plain JSON — no effect list, no closure, no live
  `TrapMatch[]`. Reader: `owedWindowOf(resume)` (exported, defensive, since the
  payload comes back through `JSON.parse`).

    Mechanics:
    - `dispatch` (internal) now returns `TrapRun = TrapDispatch & { owed }`:
  when it stops it reports `matches.slice(index)` — the traps that never saw the
  event. A trap whose `when` declined is *not* owed (it saw the event and
  declined, R99).
    - `runTrapWindow` parks that remainder via `oweWindow` → `work.owe`. It also
  parks the **whole** matched list if a prompt is already open at the window's
  scheduled point, instead of silently returning; it parks nothing once
  `state.result !== null`.
    - `resumeWindow` + `runOwedWindow`, registered at module scope with
  `registerWorkHandler(TRAP_WINDOW_WORK, …)` (not from a test — noted your
  `registerDefaultWorkHandler` warning). It re-reads the board only to drop
  traps that have left the field (R61) and iterates **in the owed list's
  order**, not a fresh `trapsWatching` order: `trapsInOrder` keys off
  `state.active`, and with the current `turn.ts` the next turn has already
  started by the time the answer arrives, which would otherwise flip R62's
  "ending player's traps, then the opponent's".
    - Nothing touches `state.work` or `state.workCursor` directly; nothing
  drains work. `TrapDispatch`'s public shape is unchanged on purpose —
  `rulings-c.test.ts` does `expect(fireTrapsFor(...)).toEqual({ fired: [],
  paused: false })`, so `fireTrapsFor` reconstructs `{ fired, paused }` and the
  immediate path (`OWED_TO_TRAPS` in `triggers.ts`) is untouched.
  `TRAP_WINDOW_EVENTS` still withholds `turnEnded` (R100) — not undone.

    Also per your follow-up: the `TrapTrigger` doc block now states **R99**
  instead of proposing it (and `TrapTrigger` is now just `TriggerDef`, since
  `when` is declared in `script.ts`; the alias stays because 6 card files
  annotate with it), `TRAP_WINDOW_EVENTS` cites **R100**,
  `consumeTrap`/`fireTrap` cite **R61**, and `oweWindow` cites **R117**.

    ## 4. The remaining gap: `turn.ts` owes the rest of the end of turn

    `endTurn` calls `runTrapWindow` and then walks straight on to
  `runDelayed(end)`, `cleanup` and `startTurn(opponent)` without noticing the
  pause, so a delayed effect resolves *inside* an unfinished window and cleanup
  closes the turn log before the window's last traps have fired. The failing
  test's diagnostic is exact: `expected [ 'window1', 'delayed' ] to deeply equal
  [ 'window1' ]`. It cannot be fixed from `traps.ts` — `runDelayed` and
  `cleanup` are `turn.ts`-private. The fix is the same shape as the window's:
  when `state.pending !== null` after the window, park the steps after it as a
  work item of its own; parked at `state.workCursor` it lands *behind* the
  window's remainder, so the drain finishes the window first and R62's order
  survives. A long comment above the test says this, so whoever takes `turn.ts`
  sees it.

    ## 5. Second task: the dispatch frontier is now in `state.dispatch`
  (`triggers.ts`)

    `SettleSink.dispatched` is demoted to "how many of this sink's events have
  been *copied* into the frontier"; the frontier itself is `state.dispatch`,
  filled by a new `collectEvents` with `{ id: "e<seq>", seq, event }` from
  `state.nextSeq` (R68's one counter), and drained by `dispatchNewEvents`, which
  now takes each event off `state.dispatch` before offering it. It stops
  advancing while (a) a prompt is open or the game is over, or (b) an
  `OWED_TO_TRAPS` entry is queued — an event whose own trap dispatch is
  unfinished. (b) is load-bearing: without it, an event left in the frontier
  would have its traps fire *before* the earlier event's owed traps on the
  answering action, i.e. out of emission order.

    ## Two places I concluded your brief was wrong, with evidence

    **1. The board-wide verbs cannot be `TargetSpec` + a scope.**
  `resolveTarget` returns a single `DamageTarget | null`, so every verb written
  in a `TargetSpec` — `damage`, `destroy`, `buff`, `transform` — is
  single-target by construction. I still added the scope, as its own vocabulary
  in `targets.ts`: `BoardScope`, `cardsInScope`, `adjacentTo`, `matchesScope`,
  walking R68 order and matching top-of-Stack only (R13). Six verbs are thin
  walks over that one piece of work. It's the shape `buffAllUnits`, `stealAll`
  and `switchAllPositions` already had. I also added `{ of: "instance";
  instanceId }` to `TargetSpec` — `transform`, `vanilla`, `setRadiant` and
  `steal` had each grown a private `instanceId` arg for want of it.

    **2. `forcedAttacks`/`forcedAttacksOn` are not merely misnamed.**
  `combat.forceAttack`/`forceAttacksOn` take an `EngineSink`; a card hook has
  none. They needed thin `Effect` wrappers (which never reimplement combat), so
  bucket (b), not (c). `index.ts`'s own header claimed these were "not part of
  the card-script surface" — false, since §6.3 lists them as verbs and
  #9/#60/#96 need them. Corrected.

    You were right on both aliasing cautions. `discardHand` ≠ `discardRandom`:
  #76 replaces the whole hand with no choice, so R16 never arises, and
  `discardRandom({ count: hand.length })` would burn `hand.length` rng draws and
  move `rngCursor`, which §10.7 makes part of state — changing every downstream
  replay hash for nothing.

  now requires the heading form**, per `03_match_lifecycle.sql`'s header and

  row id written where a name goes (followed by `:` or `)`). That accepts both
  real forms — `### R104: … ###` and `=== CHECK 15 (R105): … ===` — and rejects
  prose echoes and comments.

    **The invariant is now enforced by its own test**, not just by my care:
  `it("credits an SQL row only from a heading, so R107–R109's prose disclaimer
  is not a proof")` asserts that the SQL files credit exactly R104, R105, R106,
  R110, R111, R112 and credit *nothing* for R107, R108, R109 — and it first
  asserts the disclaimer prose is still present, so it cannot go vacuous if that
  comment is ever deleted. I verified the guard is load-bearing rather than
  decorative: a substring matcher credits R107/R108/R109 from the disclaimer (1
  hit each), the heading form credits them 0. Your reasoning about which case

    ## Where the accessors went, and why

    **New file: `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine
  /src/query.ts`**, re-exported from `packages/engine/src/index.ts` with a
  one-line comment saying what it is. Card files import from `@jackioh/engine`,
  which is already how they get `activeUnitsOf`, `cardAt`, `slotsOf`, `defOf`,
  `findInstance`, `faceOf`, `statsWithBuffs` — so nothing new had to be wired
  and no parallel surface exists.

    Not `zones.ts`, for three reasons: `zones.ts` is a mutator module
  (`placeOnField`, `moveToZone`, `lockZone`, `resetInstance`) whose readers are
  there because they read the thing it writes; a hero block and a turn log are
  not zones at all and would have no home there; and putting a read-only surface
  among the writers hides the one property that makes it a surface.
  `src/query.ts` is now the read half of the card-facing contract, sitting
  opposite `src/effects/index.ts`, the write half. The header notes the naming
  hazard (`catalog.ts` owns §5.1's card-pool query, wrapped for cards by
  `packages/cards/src/query.ts`; this module queries the board) and neither
  exports a bare `query`.

    ## The accessor list

    | accessor | returns |
    | --- | --- |
    | `heroOf(state, player)` | `HeroView` = `{ readonly health, readonly armor
  }`, a copy |
    | `zoneCards(state, player, zone)` | `readonly CardInstance[]`, a fresh
  copy, `library[0]` first |
    | `zoneCount(state, player, zone)` | `number` |
    | `cardsPlayedThisTurn(state, player)` | `number` — §10.5 step 4's counter |
    | `playedIdsThisTurn(state, player)` | `readonly string[]`, a fresh copy, in
  play order |
    | `wasPlayedThisTurn(state, player, card \| instanceId)` | `boolean` |

    `zone` reuses `zones.ts`'s existing `OffFieldZone` (`"hand" | "library" |
  "graveyard" | "exile"`) rather than inventing a second zone union. The
  zone→pile mapping stays private to the module because handing a card file a
  live `CardInstance[]` hands it a `push` into a zone.

    One design note worth your attention: **`wasPlayedThisTurn` takes an
  explicit `player`.** #23 and #24 read the log of `self.controller`, #31 reads
  `self.owner`. Collapsing that into a card-only signature would have silently
  picked one, so each call site keeps its own player expression verbatim — zero
  behaviour change, and the caller still says which log it means.

  the resolved instance can honour that. So the loop has to live inside one
  `apply`.

  I extended the existing verb rather than adding a second barrel name:
  `fuseCards({ defIds?, instanceIds?, targetInstanceId?, targetInstanceIds?,
  pick?: "random"|"all", toHand? })`. Ingredients resolve **once** and those
  same objects are reused for each fusion; `targetInstanceId` is unchanged so
  every existing call site is unaffected. This is also the shape #85's own
  author proposed. Your R86 reasoning is in the doc comment — R86 degrades a
  *pool* draw, an `instanceIds` entry is an instruction.

  ## Item 2 — the `state.dispatch` frontier (`triggers.ts`)

  `SettleSink.dispatched` is demoted to "how many of this sink's events have
  been **copied** into the frontier". The frontier is now `state.dispatch`,
  filled by a new `collectEvents` as `{ id: "e<seq>", seq, event }` from
  `state.nextSeq`, and drained by `dispatchNewEvents`, which takes each event
  **off** `state.dispatch` before offering it. It stops advancing while (a) a
  prompt is open or the game is over, or (b) an `OWED_TO_TRAPS` entry is queued
  — an event whose own trap dispatch is unfinished. (b) is load-bearing: without
  it, a leftover event's traps would fire *before* the earlier event's owed
  traps on the answering action, i.e. out of emission order.

  actor half was already right (`protocol.ts` rebuilds the body field by field
  so the wire's `playerId` never reaches `reduce`; the row was stamped `p1`).
  The mismatch was the refusal *reason*: the fake engine tested "a prompt is
  open" before "whose turn is it", so p2's out-of-turn `endTurn` was answered "a
  prompt is open: answer it first" — a refusal that describes the other seat's
  business instead of the asker's own (§9.1). Fix in `test/fakes/engine.ts`:
  with a prompt open, a player who is not the active player hears only "it is
  not your turn"; only the active player is told a prompt is in the way.

    **4. "answers a malformed frame and stays alive" — FIXED, and this one is an
  assertion correction I want you to see.** The malformed handling was already
  right (three `error`/`malformed` frames, socket stays open, next action acks
  at seq 1). The expectation `toEqual({ nonce: "after-garbage", seq: 1 })` was
  **unsatisfiable**: the helper is `socket.ofType("ack")`, which matches a frame
  only if it carries `type: "ack"`, so an ack without the discriminator could
  never be returned by that helper at all — and the same file's error assertion
  (line 406) requires `type: "error"` to be *present*. The two claims cannot
  both hold. I made the two ack expectations name the whole frame (`{ type:
  "ack", nonce, seq }`) rather than drop a field, and widened the
  `acks()`/`errors()` generics to include `type` so the helpers describe what
  `ofType` actually returns. Same strength, still `toEqual`, no `toMatchObject`.
  The alternative — stripping `type` inside the fake's `ofType` — would have
  broken the error assertion and made the protocol's tagged union untestable.

  says "rate-limit **the socket**", and only the per-socket reading is safe — a
  shared counter lets a flooding player spend the *opponent's* budget and have
  the victim's legitimate clicks refused, turning the anti-abuse limit into the
  abuse. Proposed: *"§9.8's action limit is enforced per seat: each socket gets
  R109's 5 actions per second, so a match's aggregate ceiling is twice that
  number and neither player can consume the other's budget."*

    Pre-existing `NOT IN SPEC:` markers in my files, none settled by
  R79/R105/R110/R111/R112:
    2. `actor.ts` — `disconnectExpired` is stamped with the *disconnected*
  player's seat (the loss is theirs) rather than the active seat, so a fold
  reads one seat and never "whoever happened to be active".
    3. `actor.ts` — `ceilingReached` belongs to neither player; stamped as the
  active seat so a fold never guesses. (R79 makes the ceiling a draw, R112
  covers the reaper's version; neither fixes the seat.)
    4. `clock.ts` — a second `startGrace` before `clearGrace` keeps the first
  deadline, so a flapping socket cannot extend its own grace window
  indefinitely.
    5. `wsServer.ts` — close codes 4401/4403/4404/1011 as private-use mirrors of
  the HTTP statuses.
    6. `rooms.ts` — `CODE_ATTEMPTS = 8` collision retries before `unavailable`
  (R110 settles code *reuse*, not the retry count).

    ## The helper

    `heroArmorOf(state, player): number` in `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Program
  ming/JackiOh/packages/engine/src/damage.ts`, directly above `heroDamageCap`
  and exported through the engine index (`export * from "./damage"`). It sums
  the hero's stored `armor` with every backrow card whose `heroArmor` static
  flag is set, each contributing the `HERO_ARMOR` value its own instance
  selects:

    ```ts
    return slotsOf(player, "backrow")
      .map((ref) => cardAt(state, ref))
      .reduce((sum, card) => {
        if (card === null || flagsOf(card).heroArmor !== true) return sum;
        const side = card.radiant ? HERO_ARMOR.radiant : HERO_ARMOR.base;
        return sum + (card.embiggened === true ? side.embiggen : side.paid);
      }, state.players[player].hero.armor);
    ```

    Four supporting edits, all inside my ownership:
    - `packages/engine/src/config.ts` — `HERO_ARMOR = { base: { paid: 2,
  embiggen: 5 }, radiant: { paid: 4, embiggen: 10 } } as const`, beside
  `ANTI_ONESHOT_CAP` (§8 row 84's four numbers; no number lives in the card
  file, per BUILD §2).
    - `packages/engine/src/script.ts` — `heroArmor?: boolean` in `StaticFlags`.
  I kept it a boolean rather than "better-typed": #73's `antiOneshot` +
  `ANTI_ONESHOT_CAP` is the exact precedent, and a flag carrying its own numbers
  would put rules constants in a card file. R124 makes it a layer, not a value,

    ## `cardResolved` in `redactEvent`

    It joined the **first** group of the switch — the card-naming events that
  carry both `instanceId` and `defId` (`cardPlayed`, `summoned`, `drawn`,
  `trapFired`, …) — so it returns `hidden(event.instanceId) ? { ...event,
  instanceId: HIDDEN_ID, defId: HIDDEN_ID } : event`. Per R97 it therefore
  routes through `mayRead` and reads openly in the ordinary case (a resolved
  Spell is in the public graveyard, a resolved permanent on the public field),
  with the sentinel reserved for a card that ended up somewhere the viewer may
  not read — a Trap set face-down, or a card resolved back into a hand or
  library. `player` and `permanent` are never redacted (`permanent` is R61's
  "still in play" answer for #85). The switch is still exhaustive with **no
  `default`**; one wrinkle worth knowing for the next person: eslint's
  `no-fallthrough` reports a comment sitting *between* two case labels, so the
  explanation lives in the group's leading comment block rather than immediately
  above `case "cardResolved"`.

    ### Engine changes

    `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine/src/playCho
  ices.ts`
    - New exported `playsOnStack(state, card)`: `hasKeyword(faceOf(state,
  card).keywords, "Stack")`, guarded by `needsZone` and `rowForCard(...) ===
  "units"`. **`faceOf`, not `unitView`** — `unitView` is the field reading: it
  adds `grantedKeywords` and layer-5 auras, and an aura's `applies` predicate
  reads instance data only (it does not check zone), so a "your units have …"
  aura could hand a keyword to a card sitting in a hand. `faceOf` is the
  radiant-aware printed text, which is all a card in hand has (no effect in the
  set writes `grantedKeywords` off the field, and R78 clears them on the way
  out).
    - New private `acceptsStack(state, ref)`: `row === "units" && !isLocked &&
  !isReserved`. Occupancy is exactly the refusal Stack lifts, so what is left is
  the two it never covered — R64's lock and Reborn reservation both still
  refuse.
    - `legalZonesFor` now returns `slotsOf(player, row).filter(acceptsStack)`
  for a Stack card, `openZones` otherwise.
    - `refuseZone` now branches on the same pair of predicates (`playsOnStack ?
  acceptsStack : isOpen`), keeping the existing `that ${row} zone is not open`
  message so the "locked zone rejects play" tests still match.

    `/Users/jgoetzmann/Documents/Programming/JackiOh/packages/engine/src/playSte
  ps.ts` — placement step only: `placeOnField(state, card, run.zone, { stack:
  playsOnStack(state, card) })`. Nothing else in that file touched.

    Both functions are pure; no `Math.random`, no `Date`.

    ### Harness keys added (`packages/cards/test/_harness.ts`)
    - **`FieldEntry.stack?: boolean`** (unit zones only). Permits a repeated
  `lane`; with no `lane` it lands on the entry before it in the list. Later
  entries go on top, as a play would put them, so the pile reads top-first and
  the list reads bottom-first: `field: ["core-043", { def: "core-092", stack:
  true }]` is a Fiender over a dormant Big Felinor in lane 1. `assignLanes` was
  rewritten to one ordered pass; a repeated lane *without* the flag still throws
  `two cards were given lane N`, now with `— add \`stack: true\` to entry [i]
  for a §3.2 Stack pile` appended (the existing `_harness.test.ts` regex still
  matches). `stack: true` with nothing under it, or in the backrow, throws a
  named error rather than quietly making no pile.

    ### One rule SPEC does not make — wording for you to decide
    **A Stack card played with no named zone.** I left the default alone: §3.2's
  "A summon with no named zone goes to the leftmost **empty**, unlocked zone"
  (R64), so a Stack card that names no zone still takes the leftmost empty zone
  and is refused `no free units zone` on a full board — even though
  `legalZonesFor` would offer it five stackable lanes. The asymmetry is only in
  the zone-less convenience path; a *named* zone agrees in both directions,
  which is what R81/R90 govern. It also sits in `validatePlay`'s `firstFreeZone`
  call, which is outside the placement step I was given, so I did not touch it.

    Proposed §3.2 sentence, if you want the convenience path to stack: *"A Stack
  card played with no named zone still takes the leftmost empty, unlocked zone
  (R64); it stacks only onto a zone the play names, so a full row refuses a
  zone-less Stack play."* — That is what the code does today. The alternative
  ("…and when no zone is empty it stacks onto the leftmost unlocked zone") would
  need a one-line change in `playSteps.validatePlay`, which is not mine. Do not
  let me pick the R-number; §11 is at R136 and it is being appended to live.
